The final step in the pathway links Faropenem medoxomil to EC-GI-10, suggesting that the antibacterial activity of Faropenem medoxomil could be modulated by DSK. This implies that lovastatin may influence the activity of DSK, which in turn could affect the interaction between Faropenem medoxomil and EC-GI-10. The evidence supports a possible regulatory or modulatory role of lovastatin on the pathway involving DSK and Faropenem medoxomil, ultimately influencing EC-GI-10. The strength of the evidence is moderate, as it is based on a single score and a single pathway, and further experimental validation would be necessary to confirm the proposed mechanism.
